measures.title: Licensure of Large Retailers to Finance a Clean Energy Fund
measures.summary: Asks whether Eugene voters should adopt an ordinance that, beginning January 1, 2029, requires large retailers to obtain a city license and pay an annual 2% fee on gross profits from retail sales in Eugene. A large retailer is one with more than $1 billion in gross profits nationally and $500,000 in Eugene, excluding contractors, utilities, cooperatives and credit unions; most groceries, medicines, residential garbage and recycling, and health care are not counted. The money would go to a Eugene Clean Energy Fund for renewable energy and efficiency programs, clean energy job training, green infrastructure, innovation and administration (capped at 10% from 2030), guided by an expert committee.
measures.yesMeans: Large retailers in Eugene must be licensed and pay a 2% fee on Eugene retail gross profits starting in 2029, funding a city clean energy fund.
measures.noMeans: The large-retailer license and 2% fee are not adopted.
